o: Identify the purposes of three OCR J277 utilities.
Explain how defragmentation applies to magnetic hard disks.
Select appropriate utilities for privacy and storage scenarios.
c: Utility software performs additional housekeeping, maintenance and protection tasks which might not be performed directly by the operating system.
Encryption changes readable plaintext into ciphertext using an algorithm/key, protecting data if it is accessed without authorisation. A suitable key is needed to decrypt it.
Compression reduces the storage space needed for data. Lossless allows exact reconstruction; lossy removes information and is unsuitable when exact recovery is needed.

On a magnetic hard disk, fragments of a file may be scattered. Defragmentation puts file parts together so the read head needs fewer movements. SSDs should not be routinely defragmented for this purpose.

m.title: Explain magnetic disk defragmentation
m.q: A school library's magnetic hard disk has become fragmented. Explain how defragmentation can improve file access. [4 marks]
st: Identify the storage medium: a magnetic hard disk.
Parts of files may be scattered in separate locations on disk [1].
Defragmentation rearranges these parts into adjacent blocks [1], reducing movement of the disk read/write head [1].
Less movement can reduce time accessing the file [1]. Do not suggest this improves SSD read-head movement.

w: A business stores confidential customer records on portable media. Explain why encryption software is suitable. [4 marks]
Encryption turns readable data into ciphertext [1] using an algorithm/key [1]. If the device is lost or stolen [1], the records cannot readily be understood without the correct decryption key [1].
A podcaster wants to reduce the size of large audio files and accepts some lost quality. Explain a suitable utility and one drawback. [4 marks]
Compression software reduces file size [1], saving storage or transfer time [1]. Lossy compression discards some data [1], so the original sound cannot be perfectly reconstructed [1].
A school has an SSD and a magnetic hard disk. Explain why defragmentation may help the HDD but is not normally useful for the SSD. [4 marks]

On an HDD files can be fragmented [1], making the mechanical read/write head move between locations [1]. Defragmentation groups parts and reduces head movement [1]; SSDs have no moving read/write head, so this benefit does not apply [1].

k.q: Model a simple four-to-one size reduction to estimate storage saved by compression.
k.code:
originalKb = 240
compressedKb = 60
savedKb = originalKb - compressedKb
print(savedKb)
p: Predict how many KB are saved.
Change compressedKb to 80 and calculate the new saving.
Add a selection statement that prints "Smaller" if compressedKb is less than originalKb.
k.a:
Original output: 180 KB. With compressedKb = 80: 160 KB.

Extension:
originalKb = 240
compressedKb = 80
savedKb = originalKb - compressedKb
print(savedKb)
if compressedKb < originalKb then
    print("Smaller")
endif

Outputs: 160; Smaller. This simulates the size saving; it does not implement a compression algorithm.

A doctor encrypts confidential files on a portable drive. Explain TWO reasons this helps keep information private. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.

Encryption transforms readable data into ciphertext [1], preventing straightforward reading [1]. A decryption key is needed [1], so losing the drive does not automatically expose readable records [1].

A school is choosing utility software. Explain when compression, encryption and defragmentation may each be useful. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style teaching question; not an official past-paper question.

Compression reduces file size [1] to save storage or transfer time [1]. Encryption converts data to unreadable ciphertext [1], protecting content from unauthorised access [1]. Defragmentation reorganises fragmented HDD files [1] and can reduce mechanical disk access time [1].
v: Programs performing additional maintenance or protection tasks.
Converts plaintext into ciphertext using an algorithm and key.
Converts encrypted data back to readable form with the required key.
Reduces how much storage data requires.
Rearranges fragmented file parts on a magnetic hard disk.
Parts of a file stored in separated locations on disk.
Secondary storage device using rotating magnetic platters.
x: Defragmentation is mainly intended to reduce mechanical read-head movement on fragmented magnetic hard disks.
r: State the purpose of a device driver. [2 marks]
Software that enables an operating system to communicate [1] with a specific hardware device/peripheral [1].
State TWO functions of an operating system. [2 marks]
Provides a user interface [1]; allocates/manages RAM for applications [1]. Other valid functions include file, device, user management and multitasking.
Why must a source-code file use lossless instead of lossy compression? [2 marks]
Lossless compression retains all original data [1], so source code can be reconstructed exactly with no missing characters [1].
A photographer switches between photo-editing software and a browser. Explain how operating-system memory management and multitasking support this. [4 marks]
OS allocates RAM to each program [1] so needed data is available [1]. It manages the running tasks and processor time [1], so the user can switch between programs while both remain active [1].

priorExam.q: A hotel has guest and manager accounts on one shared computer. Explain how user management prevents guests from changing booking records. [4 marks]
priorExam.a: OS assigns different user accounts [1] and can authenticate the person signing in [1]. Access rights restrict guest permissions [1], so only authorised staff can edit booking records [1].
